test_title: PYST 56: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: By selling an article at (4)/(13) of its actual selling price, Hitesh incurs a loss of 22%. If he sells it at 60% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Actual SP = 13 units.

⇒ SP₁ = 4 units = 78% of CP (since 22% loss) ⇒ 1 unit = 19.5% of CP

⇒ SP₂ = 60% of Actual SP = 0.60 × 13 units = 7.8 units

⇒ SP₂ in terms of CP = 7.8 × 19.5% = 152.1% of CP

⇒ Profit % = 152.1% − 100% = 52.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 52.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling at 4/13 of actual SP results in a 22% loss.

New selling condition: 60% of actual SP.

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 
• 
 
• 
 
 × 4/13
 × 60%

 
 Actual SP = 253.5% of CP

 
 SP₁ = 78% of CP
 (22% Loss)

 
 SP₂ = 152.1% of CP
 (52.1% Profit)

 New Profit = 152.1% − 100% = 52.1%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x

⇒ New SP₁ = 100x × (100 − 22) ÷ 100 = 78x

⇒ According to the question: 4/13 of Actual SP = 78x

⇒ Actual SP = 78x × 13 ÷ 4 = 253.5x

⇒ Now, the article is sold at 60% of Actual SP.

⇒ New SP₂ = 60% of 253.5x = (60 ÷ 100) × 253.5x = 152.1x

⇒ Profit = New SP₂ − CP = 152.1x − 100x = 52.1x

⇒ Profit % = (52.1x ÷ 100x) × 100 = 52.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 52.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective discount percentage is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a dealer claims to sell at cost price but uses a false weight, Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
